chernobyl_use_1986: Primary Soviet gamma dose rate instrument used by liquidators and emergency responders 1986; DP-5 range: 0.05 mR/hr to 200 R/hr (0.0005 µSv/hr to 1760 µSv/hr equivalent); when dose rate exceeded 200 R/hr: meter DEFLECTED TO ZERO (pegged off-scale); in Unit 4 reactor hall night of April 26: dose rates 1000-15,000 R/hr → DP-5 showed 0 → operators initially concluded reactor was not badly damaged; only one 'off-scale' high dose meter (1000 R/hr range) available and used; critical failure: responders reporting '3.6 R/hr' (max reading on one instrument) when actual levels were 15,000+ R/hr
limitations_observed: DP-5 systematic underestimation: designed for peacetime nuclear fallout monitoring and routine plant monitoring; not designed for post-accident extreme dose rates; saturation at 200 R/hr gave false '0' reading = most dangerous failure mode (responders thought environment was safe); Bryukhanov reported '3.6 R/hr' to Moscow based on surviving meter reading; actual maximum measured by high-range dosimeter: 1000 R/hr (off-scale on that too); actual room 305/2 and reactor hall: 15,000+ R/hr; consequence: initial response (no evacuation; no KI distribution) based on faulty dosimetry

chernobyl_use_1986: KID-2 (Квантовый Индивидуальный Дозиметр): personal dosimeter worn by liquidators; glass ionization chamber; 0-5 rem (0-50 mSv) range; read by operator at end of shift; PROBLEM: most liquidators received doses that rapidly exceeded 5 rem → meter maxed out → could not record further exposure; Soviet occupational limit = 35 rem/year (350 mSv); KID-2 maxes out in 7 visits at full limit; supervisors: confiscated KID-2 when workers reached 35 rem (workers transferred to non-radiation work; replacement workers sent); systemic falsification: in many units: KID-2 readings reduced ('corrected') in records to keep workers under official limit → enabled continued work
limitations_observed: KID-2 failures documented by post-hoc EPR dosimetry: tooth enamel EPR studies show actual doses 1.5-3× KID-2 records for most liquidators; roof workers: actual doses up to 15× KID-2 records; WHY falsified: (1) supervisors needed work done; replacement workers = planning failure; (2) workers themselves sometimes covered meter (to avoid losing income); (3) supervisors ordered adjustments; (4) some units: all KID-2s assigned same value (group falsification); this systematic falsification = reason RADRUE was needed 20 years later to reconstruct actual doses using JEM + EPR + FISH + interview methods

chernobyl_use_1986: Thermoluminescent Dosimeter (TLD): LiF crystal (typically LiF:Mg,Ti = TLD-100) traps electrons in crystal lattice defects upon radiation exposure; reading: heat crystal to 200-400°C → electrons released → luminescence proportional to dose; sensitivity: 0.01 mSv; upper limit: ~10 Sv (saturation above); accuracy: ±5-15% for calibrated systems; used at Chernobyl: liquidator badge TLDs alongside KID-2; at hospitals: patient dosimetry; at plant: area dosimetry; TLDs more accurate than film badge (less energy-dependent); modern use: primary personal dosimetry worldwide
limitations_observed: TLD problems at Chernobyl: (1) many workers didn't wear TLD (or wore one for whole shift in non-representative location); (2) TLD confiscated/replaced by supervisors; (3) heat during summer fieldwork → spurious signal; (4) TLD not rechargeable → workers 'forgot' them; (5) gamma-sensitive but not neutron-sensitive without special chips; (6) readings lost in poor record-keeping during chaotic 1986-1990 period; EPR tooth enamel retrospective dosimetry = used to validate/correct TLD records; Chernobyl: TLD records should be treated as LOWER BOUND on actual dose

chernobyl_use_1986: HPGe (High-Purity Germanium) detector: semiconductor; band gap 0.7 eV; 662 keV photon → ~9×10⁵ electron-hole pairs; energy resolution FWHM = 1.9-2.5 keV at 1332 keV (Co-60) = 100-200× better than NaI(Tl); operates at liquid nitrogen temperature (77K) or Peltier cooling (modern); efficiency: relative to 3×3 inch NaI = 15-100%; applications at Chernobyl: soil sample analysis; food monitoring (Cs-137; Cs-134; Ru-106; Ba-140; Zr-95); Am-241 measurement in soil (59.5 keV gamma; 35.7% yield); HPGe essential because Cs-137 (662 keV) and I-131 (365 keV) are close to Cs-134 lines (563/569/604/796 keV) = NaI cannot resolve; HPGe baseline required for contamination studies
limitations_observed: HPGe enabled: (1) Cs-134/Cs-137 ratio determination (forensic fingerprint); (2) Am-241 measurement as Pu-241 → Am-241 tracking; (3) food contamination beyond EU limits detection; (4) source term reconstruction from early air samples; mobile HPGe units deployed to CEZ 1986 onward for environmental characterization; current 2026: all European monitoring stations with laboratory HPGe; many field HPGe (liquid nitrogen or Peltier-cooled portable); CTBTO IMS stations use HPGe as primary detector

chernobyl_use_1986: NaI(Tl) scintillation detector: thallium-doped sodium iodide crystal; photon → photoelectron → scintillation photons → photomultiplier tube → signal; energy resolution: FWHM ~50-80 keV at 662 keV (NaI) vs 2 keV (HPGe); adequate for dose rate measurement (all gammas counted) and gross contamination; inadequate for isotope discrimination at complex CEZ gamma spectrum; typical Soviet instruments using NaI: SRP-68-01 (search instrument; sensitivity to Cs-137 40,000 cps per µR/s); BDKG-41 (NaI probe for SRP-88); modern field monitors: GAMMA-SCOUT; Inspector Alert; Mirion RDS-31; all use NaI or CsI scintillators for field gamma rate
limitations_observed: NaI at Chernobyl: SRP-68-01 used for contamination surveys 1986-1991; dose rate measurement; adequate for mapping overall gamma contamination but cannot distinguish isotopes; in food monitoring: NaI appropriate for screening (detect >EU limit) but confirmation requires HPGe; self-settler thyroid scanning 1986: special thyroid NaI collimated probe directed at neck to measure I-131 in thyroid gland; WBC NaI array (4π geometry) for Cs-137 body burden: standard method used 1990-2026 in Ukrainian health monitoring programs

chernobyl_use_1986: Geiger-Müller (GM) tube: gas-filled tube (typically Ar/He + halogen quench); avalanche multiplication gives large pulse regardless of photon energy; ADVANTAGE: simple; robust; cheap; DISADVANTAGE: no energy discrimination; at high count rates (>10⁵ cps): dead time → saturation; common Soviet/civilian instruments: SBM-20 tube (used in Chernobyl); Dosimetro-2B; civil defense DP-3B; modern Geiger counters: RadiaCode; GQ GMC-600; Mazur PRM-9000; ECOTEST Terra-P; GM energy response: varies (efficiency 10-30% for Cs-137 662 keV); adequate for hot spot finding and dose rate monitoring in expected environments
limitations_observed: GM detectors at Chernobyl: first instruments deployed by firefighters and emergency responders; measured hot spots on reactor roof; most robust for field conditions; limitation: when measuring Sr-90 (pure beta; 2.28 MeV max from Y-90): GM detects beta particles if using thin-window probe; but without thin window: Cs-137 gamma dominates; Sr-90 soil contamination NOT measurable by gamma-only instruments; SaveEcoBot network (2016-2026): uses NaI-based monitors + Geiger tubes; real-time data API; 200+ stations across Ukraine; Prypiat current reading 4.932 µSv/hr = from Cs-137 gamma measured by NaI + GM combination

chernobyl_use_1986: EPR (Electron Paramagnetic Resonance) tooth enamel dosimetry: extracted tooth enamel (hydroxyapatite Ca₁₀(PO₄)₆(OH)₂) ground to powder; EPR spectrometer measures radiation-induced radical signal; signal proportional to absorbed dose (Gy); detection limit: 34 mGy with 1g sample (analytical precision); signal PERMANENT in crystal lattice (unlike RPL or TLD which can fade); therefore: archival record of LIFETIME cumulative dose; X-ray/dental radiograph correction required; background native signal subtracted; Chernobyl application: 2800 liquidators + 300 evacuees had EPR dosimetry performed; compared to KID-2/TLD records: EPR consistently higher (confirms systematic badge underestimation)
limitations_observed: EPR validation of RADRUE: EPR group mean doses within 10-25% of RADRUE JEM-based estimates; individual correlation r=0.35-0.55 (moderate; expected given biological variation); Ukrainian/Russian EPR studies (Sholom 2000; Skvortsov 2000; Jacob 1999): established EPR as gold standard for retrospective dosimetry of liquidators above 100 mGy; EPR national programs: RADOSYS program in Germany; French IRSN studies; EPR used for: Chernobyl occupational dose verification; Fukushima workers (2011-2016); nuclear test site populations; mining accident populations; dose reconstruction for compensation programs

chernobyl_use_1986: EURDEP (European Radiological Data Exchange Platform): automated data exchange network; operated by JRC (Joint Research Centre); >5000 monitoring stations across 39 European countries; data: gamma dose rate H*(10); some: aerosol filters; noble gas; precipitation sampling; real-time: 10-minute update frequency; public access: eurdep.ec.europa.eu; 2026 coverage: continuous monitoring across Europe; any release comparable to Chernobyl detected within 30-60 minutes; Ukraine war impact: ~40% of Ukrainian monitoring network in occupied/conflict territory; SNRIU-operated stations continue where accessible; SaveEcoBot commercial network: fills gaps in Ukrainian coverage
limitations_observed: EURDEP capability vs 1986: in 1986 = <200 manual radiation stations in Western Europe; no automated data exchange; Forsmark detected Chernobyl April 28 (2 days after accident) through manual contamination monitoring; 2026: 5000+ automated stations with 10-min reporting → any similar release detected within 30-60 min; detection threshold for Cs-137: ~0.001 µSv/hr above background = detectable at 1000+ km distance for major release; EURDEP + CTBTO IMS = dual detection network; EURDEP (environmental gamma) + CTBTO (atmospheric samples including noble gas) = complete early warning system
